title: Tight regret bound for Hedge's convex predictions
statement:
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set, let $\eta > 0$ be a learning rate, and consider a prediction problem with $N \ge 1$ experts over $T$ rounds, an outcome $o_t$ at each round $t$, and a loss function $\ell(x, o)$. Suppose that every expert prediction $p_t(i)$ lies in $S$, that for each round $t$ the map $x \mapsto \ell(x, o_t)$ is convex on $S$, and that the induced loss sequence is valid, so that each expert's per-round loss $\ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ lies in $[0,1]$. Then the cumulative loss $\mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T = \sum_{t} \ell(\widehat{x}_t, o_t)$ of Hedge's weighted-average predictions $\widehat{x}_t$ exceeds the best expert loss in hindsight $L^* = \min_{i} \sum_{t} \ell(p_t(i), o_t)$ by at most
\[
  \mathcal{L}^{\mathrm{pred}}_T - L^* \;\le\; \frac{\ln N}{\eta} + \frac{\eta T}{8}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: S is a convex subset of the reals
every expert prediction lies in S
each round's loss is convex in the prediction on S
the induced loss sequence is valid (per-round losses in [0,1])
